paragraphs: Swamiji had a sharp sense of humour about people who make a show of their principles. Here is one of his stories about a man who was very proud of never harming any living thing.

One night a thief broke into this man's house. The young men of the household caught him and started giving him a thorough thrashing. Hearing all the noise, the master stepped out onto the upstairs balcony, found out what was going on, and called down to them to stop at once. Don't beat him, he told them; not hurting others is the highest virtue.
His obedient young followers in non-violence immediately stopped. Then they looked up and asked what they should do with the thief instead.

The master gave his order: tie him up in a sack and throw him into the water. And the thief, deeply grateful for such gentle treatment, folded his hands and exclaimed, "Oh! How great is the master's compassion!"
learn: It is easy to follow the letter of a rule and completely miss its spirit. Before you feel good about sticking to your principles, check whether you are actually being kind or just looking like it. Real values show in results, not in slogans.
